title: Everyone else is shrinking satellites. K2 raised $500m to build giant ones, and put AI in orbit.
excerpt: Most satellite startups are racing to build smaller. K2 Space is going the other way, on purpose. Investors just handed it $500 million to keep going bigger. K2 raised a $500 million Series D at a $6.8 billion valuation, it said on Thursday
content_html:
Most satellite startups are racing to build smaller. K2 Space is going the other way, on purpose. Investors just handed it $500 million to keep going bigger.

K2 raised a $500 million Series D at a $6.8 billion valuation, it said on Thursday. Kleiner Perkins and ICONIQ led the round, with Alphabet’s CapitalG, Lightspeed and ARK Invest among the backers. That more than doubles the $3 billion valuation it carried months ago. K2 has now raised over $1 billion, against more than $1 billion in signed contracts.

The bet is contrarian. Most of the industry shrinks satellites to cut launch costs. K2 argues the opposite: in orbit, power decides what a satellite can do, so it builds big, high-power ones instead.

The proof is already up there

Its first “mega-class” satellite, Gravitas, reached orbit in March on a SpaceX Falcon 9. It weighs two tonnes, generates 20 kilowatts, and carried a dozen payloads for customers including the US military, GeekWire reported.

K2 builds more than 85% of each satellite itself. Its 180,000-square-foot factory in Torrance, California is designed to turn out up to 100 satellites a year. That in-house model, it says, is how it makes large satellites quickly and cheaply.

Defence is writing the cheques

Much of the pull is military. K2 will supply 30 satellites for SES’s meoSphere network, build spacecraft for the Anduril-led Golden Dome missile-defence programme, and act as bus provider on a US Space Force satcom effort, its first Pentagon programme of record. It fits a wider surge of money into defence space.

The real moonshot: data centres in orbit

The bigger bet sits further out. In late 2028, K2 plans a 100-kilowatt “Giga” satellite built to carry “massive amounts of compute on orbit.” In plain terms, that is a step toward AI data centres in space, an application its chief executive flagged to Bloomberg.

K2 was founded in 2022 by the brothers Karan and Neel Kunjur, the latter a former SpaceX engineer. The round lands amid a flood of money into space, from launch to defence to orbital infrastructure.

The risks are real. Building 100 large satellites a year is a manufacturing feat no one has pulled off, and space-based data centres remain years away and unproven. K2’s next mission, Trinity, flies multiple satellites in early 2027. Going from one satellite to hundreds is the bet. Whether orbit becomes the next data-centre site is the wager beyond it.

content_html_zh:
大多数卫星初创公司都在竞相建造更小的卫星。 K2 Space 故意走相反的路。 投资者刚刚向其注资 5 亿美元，以继续发展壮大。

K2 周四表示，以 68 亿美元的估值筹集了 5 亿美元的 D 轮融资。 Kleiner Perkins 和 ICONIQ 领投此轮融资，支持者包括 Alphabet 旗下的 CapitalG、Lightspeed 和 ARK Invest。 这比几个月前 30 亿美元的估值增加了一倍多。 K2 目前已筹集超过 10 亿美元，而已签署的合同则超过 10 亿美元。

这个赌注是逆向的。 大多数行业都缩小卫星尺寸以降低发射成本。 K2 的观点恰恰相反：在轨道上，功率决定卫星的功能，因此它建造了大型、高功率的卫星。

证据已经在上面了

其第一颗“巨型”卫星 Gravitas 于 3 月搭乘 SpaceX Falcon 9 号进入轨道。 据 GeekWire 报道，它重 2 吨，发电 20 千瓦，可为包括美国军方在内的客户携带十几个有效载荷。

每颗卫星 85% 以上的部件均由 K2 自行制造。 其位于加利福尼亚州托兰斯的工厂占地 180,000 平方英尺，设计年产量可达 100 颗卫星。 该公司表示，这种内部模式就是它快速、廉价地制造大型卫星的方法。

国防部正在开支票

大部分的吸引力来自军事。 K2 将为 SES 的 meoSphere 网络提供 30 颗卫星，为 Anduril 领导的金顶导弹防御计划建造航天器，并在美国太空部队卫星通信项目（其第一个五角大楼项目记录）中担任总线提供商。 它适合将更广泛的资金投入国防领域。

真正的登月计划：轨道上的数据中心

更大的赌注则更遥远。 K2 计划在 2028 年末建造一颗 100 千瓦的“Giga”卫星，用于“在轨道上进行大量计算”。 简单来说，这是向太空人工智能数据中心迈出的一步，其首席执行官向彭博社标记了这一应用程序。

K2 由 Karan Kunjur 和 Neel Kunjur 兄弟于 2022 年创立，后者是 SpaceX 的前工程师。 该轮融资伴随着大量资金涌入太空，从发射到防御再到轨道基础设施。

风险是真实存在的。 每年建造 100 颗大型卫星是一项无人能实现的制造壮举，而天基数据中心仍需数年时间才能建成且尚未得到证实。 K2 的下一个任务 Trinity 将于 2027 年初发射多颗卫星。 从一颗卫星增加到数百颗卫星是我们的赌注。 轨道是否成为下一个数据中心站点是超越它的赌注。
